text:
Dude, you have to look at this thing I found in Grandma’s attic. It’s not just old; it’s *ancient*. Like, dinosaur-old. Well, maybe not dinosaur, but definitely older than my dad’s favorite video games.

It’s a recipe card for lemon bars. But here’s the weird part: the handwriting is super wobbly and fancy, like someone used a quill pen or something. And get this—Grandma says the person who wrote it died forty years ago! Forty! That means they were writing this before your mom was even born. Maybe before *my* mom was born!

I kept staring at the ink because it looks brown instead of black now. It smells like dust and vanilla, which is kinda gross but also kinda nice? I tried to copy it down so we can make them after school, but some of the words are faded. Is that "sift" or "lift"? And why did they write "do not rush" in such big letters? Did they run out of time? Or were they just really mad about lemons?

I feel like if I touch the paper too hard, it might turn into sand. Or maybe the ghost of the writer will come back and yell at us for getting the measurements wrong. We should be careful. Maybe we should whisper when we read it. Do you think ghosts like lemon bars?
